Cyber-Physical Systems

Making sense of the physical world with wearable sensors, edge AI, and connected devices.

Research Description

Overview

What can a small device infer about the physical world, and when is that evidence reliable enough to act on? We study how wearables and connected devices interpret imperfect signals while meeting limits on power, response time, and data sharing. Our work covers activity and stress recognition, fall detection, and driver awareness.

Research Thrusts

Trustworthy wearable sensing

Study how sensor quality, training-data integrity, and privacy protections affect recognition of activity and stress.

Language-assisted physical systems

Use language models to explain what sensors observed, flag uncertainty, and communicate events such as a possible fall.

Reliable connected intelligence

Study how resource-constrained edge devices can interpret signals and deliver timely alerts, including in driver-awareness monitoring.

Research Goals

Build and evaluate sensing workflows that retain useful information, communicate uncertainty, and meet the timing and resource needs of the application.

Intellectual Merit

Trace how sensor quality, model choices, and device constraints shape the reliability of a decision from measurement to alert.

Research Impact

Guide the design of wearable tools, smart environments, and monitoring systems where a missed event or false alert matters.

Selected Studies

Selected Paper: Preprint

Wearable AI across the lifecycle

Sensor data→Integrity checks→Reliable interpretation

Activity recognition depends on the quality of measurements, labels, and their alignment with descriptions. Errors in any of them can distort what a wearable system reports.

Research objectives

Identify corrupted training records and test whether cleaning them preserves useful activity information.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

Evaluate whether a model can detect corruption, locate affected records, and recover useful data as separate tasks.

Selected publications

Adaptive and Robust Data Poisoning Detection and Sanitization in Wearable IoT Systems using Large Language Models ↗

Research Relevance

This work supports more reliable activity monitoring by testing whether a system still learns from the parts of its data that remain useful.

ISARC 2025

Language models for cyber-physical systems

Physical observations→Language-assisted interpretation→Human oversight

A fall detector needs to do more than classify a sensor event: it also needs to communicate what happened and when help may be needed.

Research objectives

Study how small language models can turn fall-detection signals into useful safety messages.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

Evaluate event detection and the message that follows as separate steps, so a clear message is not mistaken for a correct detection.

Selected publications

Development of a Fall Detection and Safety Communication System Using Small Language Models ↗

Research Relevance

In a safety workflow, people need to distinguish a possible fall from a confirmed event before deciding how to respond.

IEEE COMPSAC 2024

Driver-awareness monitoring on resource-constrained devices

Camera observations→On-device processing→Driver alert

Our COMPSAC study uses a Raspberry Pi to monitor signs of driver drowsiness, such as eye closure and yawning, and issue alerts.

Research objectives

Study what a low-cost device can detect locally and how quickly it can respond.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

The prototype uses facial landmarks to track signs of reduced alertness on hardware with limited processing capacity.

Selected publication

Enhancing Road Safety through Cost-Effective, Real-Time Monitoring of Driver Awareness with Resource-Constrained IoT Devices ↗

Research Relevance

This study illustrates why edge monitoring must be evaluated for both detection accuracy and response delay.
